title: Weingart
description: A song credit set like a forme of hand-set metal type: three lines of title on a flush-left margin, a process-red running time printed underneath, brass rule, a reversed slug, small text cascading down the right. Every line is a row of single sorts, and every line's first sort is locked to the margin. Push a line and it hinges there into a staircase, each sort its own piece of lead stepping down and right from the one before; each line steps by a fraction of its own body, so the title, the rule and the slug fan out at slopes of their own while the Swiss margin they start from never moves. The sorts are solid: a staircase that comes down onto the next line shoves exactly the letters it lands on, which breaks that line into its own staircase, and so on down the forme, each sort seating with its own knock, left to right, until the run locks against the edge of the chase. Only the red, printed in its own run, crosses the black, and where they overprint the two inks make a third, darker one.
intent: After Wolfgang Weingart's Basel letterpress experiments and his stepped Typografische Monatsblätter covers (1972–73): Swiss order broken from inside the system, using the real constraints of a press, quantised steps, letterspacing and overprinting, to make new rhythm. https://neugraphic.com/weingart/weingart-text2.html
